figures.caption: Table 10. Efficiency breakdown by family. Peak ϕ across 14 architectural families. MobileCLIP establishes the efficiency ceiling (ϕ = 2.82). Legacy and massive-scale architectures offer the lowest return. PT: Pre-training data.
Fig. 1. The MPR inference protocol. MPR frames recognition as a ranking task. For each probe image, cross-modal similarity sorts SKUs by relevance, enabling zero-shot identification.

Fig. 4. The edge-centric efficiency landscape. Semantic power density (ϕ) vs. model size. Gray dots show the full population (N = 190). Blue circles mark highefficiency MobileCLIP models. Red squares indicate poor ROI. Triangles represent massive models with low density due to parameter bloat. MobileCLIP occupies the sweet spot for edge deployment.
Fig. 2. Caption refinement. Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct compresses descriptions exceeding 77 tokens into concise captions while retaining key visual attributes.

Fig. 5. Manifold collapse illustrated. Embedding projection for a representative query. The model must distinguish Chicken Corn Chowder from Chicken & Dumplings. Shared visual attributes (red) cause vectors to collapse into a narrow cone of confusion (∆θ ≈ 4◦). Dot product cannot separate them.

Table 11. The discriminative gap. Top models ranked by Recall@5. The gap ∆ = Recall@5−Recall@1 quantifies precision drop. VLMs excel at narrowing the search space (Recall@5 ≈ 94%) but struggle to rank final candidates, with gaps exceeding 17%.
Table 7. Dataset leaders. The top performers all abandon raw scraping. Aggressive filtering or WebLI signals yield the best results.

Table 8. Comparison of efficiency metrics. We evaluate three formulations on representative models. The linear metric (M1) incorrectly favors small but inaccurate models. The quadratic-accuracy metric (M2) improves ordering but lacks a principled threshold. Our SNR-based ϕ correctly identifies MobileCLIP-B as optimal by severely penalizing sub-50% models.

Fig. 3. Architecture of the MPR pipeline. The VLM encoders (fθ, gϕ) map the probe image v and catalog descriptions {ti} into a shared embedding space. We compute the cosine similarity s(v, t) to rank the 409 SKUs.
